subject: Study Skills
title: Lecture 9 - Boosting Memory and Increasing Concentration

A.cat: Lecture 9 - Boosting Memory and Increasing Concentration
A.q: Which main skill do the ten tips aim to improve?
A.explain: The ten tips are mainly for concentration. Encoding and retrieval belong to memory processing, and self-motivation is mentioned with goal setting.

A.cat: Lecture 9 - Boosting Memory and Increasing Concentration
A.q: Match each information-processing model part to its role.

rightItems.text: Has limited capacity and a trap door
Links to self-quizzing and an inactive route
Calls saved material back for review

A.explain: Sensory input enters STM, which has limited capacity and a trap door. Rehearsal moves practice and learning to LTM, while retrieval calls saved material back for review. Feedback links to self-quizzing and the inactive path.

A.cat: Lecture 9 - Boosting Memory and Increasing Concentration
A.q: How many kinds of encoding transmit information to LTM?
A.explain: Linguistic, visual, motor, and semantic encoding are the four kinds. Each kind transmits a different type of information to LTM.

A.cat: Lecture 9 - Boosting Memory and Increasing Concentration
A.q: Match each encoding type to the information it transmits.
A.explain: Linguistic encoding transmits verbal information, and visual encoding transmits image information. Motor encoding transmits muscle memory, while semantic encoding transmits emotional information and episodic memory to LTM.

A.cat: Lecture 9 - Boosting Memory and Increasing Concentration
A.q: Match each encoding type to its alternate name.
A.explain: Linguistic encoding is also called auditory coding. Visual encoding is imaginal coding, and motor encoding is physical or kinesthetic coding.

A.cat: Lecture 9 - Boosting Memory and Increasing Concentration
A.q: Which resources suit visual learners?
A.explain: Visual learners use diagrams, color, printed materials, charts, and images. Taped class sessions suit auditory learners.

A.cat: Lecture 9 - Boosting Memory and Increasing Concentration
A.q: Which strategies help auditory learners?
A.explain: Auditory learners benefit from listening, reading notes aloud, and teaching partners. Manipulatives suit tactile or kinesthetic learners.

A.cat: Lecture 9 - Boosting Memory and Increasing Concentration
A.q: Match each learning style to its main channel.
A.explain: Visual learners use charts and images. Auditory learners use recordings and read-aloud notes. Tactile/kinesthetic learners use hands-on practice.

A.cat: Lecture 9 - Boosting Memory and Increasing Concentration
A.q: Match each learning style to a suitable strategy.
A.explain: Visual learners can use charts and images. Auditory learners can tape class sessions. Tactile/kinesthetic learners can create hands-on notes.

A.cat: Lecture 9 - Boosting Memory and Increasing Concentration
A.q: Which tip advises choosing a fixed amount of study time?
A.explain: Intend to Concentrate means setting a specified study time. Knowing the duration helps maintain focus.

A.cat: Lecture 9 - Boosting Memory and Increasing Concentration
A.q: Which tip says to gather texts, notes, pens, and guides first?
A.explain: Prepare to Concentrate means having everything needed for the task. Texts, notes, pens, and study guides should be ready.

A.cat: Lecture 9 - Boosting Memory and Increasing Concentration
A.q: Use Concentration Promoting Activities recommends which action?
A.explain: This tip includes rewriting and organizing notes. It also includes diagrams, graphs, study guides, and summaries.

A.cat: Lecture 9 - Boosting Memory and Increasing Concentration
A.q: Which tip suggests changing subjects when focus fades?
options: Devise a Specific Study Plan for Studying and Learning
A.explain: Vary Your Study Activities helps when one subject is hard to sustain. Changing subjects can restore focus.

A.cat: Lecture 9 - Boosting Memory and Increasing Concentration
A.q: Which tip advises using one place only for schoolwork?
options: Devise a Specific Study Plan for Studying and Learning
A.explain: Study in a Non-Distracting Environment means choosing one place for studying. That place should be used only for schoolwork.

A.cat: Lecture 9 - Boosting Memory and Increasing Concentration
A.q: What should a study place remove?
A.explain: A non-distracting study place removes visual and auditory distractions. Goals and meals are handled by other tips.

A.cat: Lecture 9 - Boosting Memory and Increasing Concentration
A.q: Devise a Specific Study Plan for Studying and Learning includes which practice?
options: Setting a fixed study time limit
A.explain: A step-by-step plan makes concentrating easier. It also includes a textbook reading strategy.

A.cat: Lecture 9 - Boosting Memory and Increasing Concentration
A.q: What does a step-by-step study plan make easier?
A.explain: A step-by-step plan makes it easier to concentrate. It also supports using a textbook reading strategy.

A.cat: Lecture 9 - Boosting Memory and Increasing Concentration
A.q: Which tip links food choices, less sugar, and no stimulants to grades?
options: Get Plenty of Sleep at Night
Set Daily, Weekly, Monthly, and Semester Goals
A.explain: Eat Regular, Well-Balanced Meals supports concentration and grades. It advises avoiding excess sugar and caffeine and not taking stimulants.

A.cat: Lecture 9 - Boosting Memory and Increasing Concentration
A.q: Match each study-health factor to its advice.
A.explain: Students with healthier diets earn higher grades. Excess sugar and caffeine should be limited, and stimulants should not be taken.

A.cat: Lecture 9 - Boosting Memory and Increasing Concentration
A.q: Which tip warns that staying tired harms attention?
options: Get Plenty of Sleep at Night
A.explain: Get Plenty of Sleep at Night protects concentration. Fighting off sleepiness negatively affects attention.

A.cat: Lecture 9 - Boosting Memory and Increasing Concentration
A.q: What negatively affects concentration?
A.explain: Fighting off sleepiness negatively affects concentration. Adequate sleep at night supports attention.

A.cat: Lecture 9 - Boosting Memory and Increasing Concentration
A.q: Which tip recommends targets across several time periods?
options: Set Daily, Weekly, Monthly, and Semester Goals
Devise a Specific Study Plan for Studying and Learning
A.explain: Set Daily, Weekly, Monthly, and Semester Goals gives a sense of progress. Seeing movement toward goals supports concentration and self-motivation.

A.cat: Lecture 9 - Boosting Memory and Increasing Concentration
A.q: Which tip treats wandering attention as normal and suggests a short pause?
options: Set Daily, Weekly, Monthly, and Semester Goals
A.explain: Take Regular Study Breaks accepts that concentration will wander. A short planned pause helps attention return.

A.cat: Lecture 9 - Boosting Memory and Increasing Concentration
A.q: How many minutes is the suggested study break?
A.explain: The suggested break is five minutes. It is taken when concentration normally wanders.

A.cat: Lecture 9 - Boosting Memory and Increasing Concentration
A.q: Match each concentration tip to its action.

leftItems.text: Devise a Specific Study Plan for Studying and Learning
Get Plenty of Sleep at Night
Set Daily, Weekly, Monthly, and Semester Goals

A.explain: Each tip is paired with its main action, from setting a time limit to taking a five-minute pause. Together the pairs summarize the ten concentration tips.

A.cat: Lecture 9 - Boosting Memory and Increasing Concentration
A.q: Which tip uses conscious self-talk about a set study time?
A.explain: Intend to Concentrate asks you to state a fixed study period. The self-talk form is a promise to concentrate for a number of minutes.

A.cat: Lecture 9 - Boosting Memory and Increasing Concentration
A.q: Which part ends the information-processing model by supplying final results?
A.explain: The output is the model endpoint, and outcomes are its final results. The other parts are stores or pathways.
